name: Ab Testing Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing ab testing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing ab testing style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing ab testing code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing ab testing style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to ab testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Validate ab testing outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Check that ab testing terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
4. When ab testing guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Keep ab testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
6. When ab testing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
7. Before starting ab testing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop ab testing edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated ab testing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of ab testing correctness.
- Avoid introducing new ab testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for ab testing, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
